requested.title: Public SSE route has no rate limit or connection cap, and fans out O(connections) work per queue event
Unguarded stream.send inside a shared-emitter listener: one throwing handler halts delivery to every later SSE subscriber
Event-driven SSE stream sends no heartbeat, so idle viewers are dropped by the 60s proxy read timeout and reconnect in a loop
Pending-job TTL (60s) is shorter than a job's worst-case wait at the admission cap, desynchronizing the counter and defeating the 100-job limit
settle assumes one terminal event per enqueue, but queue:failed is emitted once per retry attempt
Newsletter confirm/unsubscribe capability tokens are exported to the Umami analytics backend
Timing side channel reintroduces the subscriber oracle the response shapes were built to close
An abandoned send job permanently suppresses its own retry: the `sending` claim is never released, and the loss is logged as 'sent'
Numeric newsletter env config is unvalidated: an explicit 0 is silently ignored and a negative value breaks signup entirely

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: Every mechanical claim checks out. `MochiSseConfig` (types.ts L250-253) carries only `__mochiSse` and `handler` — there is no `rateLimit` field, so the route cannot declare one. I traced the limiter wiring in Mochi.ts: `resolveLimiter()` is called in exactly two places, the `isMochiPage` branch (L889) and the `isMochiApi` branch (L1198), and `checkRouteLimit()` only at L981 and L1211. Because `buildLimiter()` — the only path that instantiates the serve-level `options.rateLimit` into `sharedGlobalLimiter` — is reached solely through `resolveLimiter()`, a global `rateLimit` genuinely would not cover SSE either; and packages/site/src/index.ts sets none. The SSE registration path (L1336-1433) never consults `routeLimiters`, and `KIND_POLICY.sse.timeout === true` causes `server.timeout(req, 0)` in requestSetup.ts L85-87, so Bun's per-request idle timeout is explicitly disabled for these streams. The site's `protection` gate only matches `/demos/protection*`, CSRF is off for `sse` kind, and the page route's limiter is `skip`-scoped to POST, so an unauthenticated client can open arbitrarily many `GET /demos/queue/events` streams (the path is not slash-mirrored for SSE, so the exact URL matches). Each one appends three handlers to the process-global mitt emitter plus a retained ReadableStream, and `push` calls `queueStatus()` (array copy + reverse) and `JSON.stringify` once per connection per event; one enqueue emits `queue:added` and `queue:completed`, so the cost is 2N. Per spec, `controller.enqueue` appends regardless of `desiredSize`, so a non-reading client also grows its stream's internal queue. Concrete attack: hold N streams from a script (no browser 6-per-host limit), then spend the 60/min POST quota — server work scales linearly in N with nothing in the app or framework to bound N. MEDIUM is appropriate for an unauthenticated, uncapped streaming endpoint with O(N) fan-out on a deployed site.

Two of the three links in this chain are confirmed, but the premise is not. Confirmed: `stream.send` reaches a bare `controller.enqueue(frame)` (Mochi.ts L1399) with no try/catch; the only deregistration path is the ReadableStream `cancel()` callback (L1417-1423) — Mochi never registers a `req.signal` abort listener; and mitt's emit really is `i.slice().map(h => h(t))` with no per-handler isolation (verified in node_modules/mitt/dist/mitt.js), while `notifySafely` (queue.ts L544-550) catches only at the whole-emit level, so a throw would silently abort delivery to every later-registered handler. What is missing is any actor that can leave a live `push` bound to a non-readable controller. Per the Streams spec, `ReadableStreamCancel` sets state to `closed` and then synchronously invokes the underlying source's cancel steps, so Mochi's `closeCallbacks` (the three `mochiEvents.off` calls) run in the same step the controller stops accepting chunks — there is no gap. The finding's alternative, 'cancel() has not yet run after the socket closed', is harmless for the opposite reason: until cancel runs the stream is still `readable`, so `enqueue` buffers instead of throwing. Its other alternative, 'a stream errored rather than cancelled', names no erroring party: this demo never calls `stream.close()` or `controller.error()`, and Bun's documented contract is that it calls the stream's `cancel()` when the client disconnects — the historical cancel-not-called bug (oven-sh/bun#8334, #14390) was fixed in Bun 1.1.27, and this repo pins 1.4.4 (.bun-version). Circumstantial support: `/sse/time` and `/sse/admin/stock` use the same blessed idiom (a `setInterval` calling `stream.send`, cleared only in `onClose`), so if `enqueue` threw on a dead controller those long-lived demos would raise an uncaught error within a second of every disconnect. The defensive try/catch plus self-deregistration is still worthwhile hardening, and the recommendation to guard `enqueue` inside the framework is sound, but no reachable failure scenario exists on the pinned runtime.

The code side is fully verified. The handler sends nothing on open and only reacts to `queue:*` events, so a visitor who reads the page without enqueuing receives zero body bytes; `MochiSseStream.send` emits only `id:`/`event:`/`data:` lines, so the framework has no comment-heartbeat or `retry:` facility; and `KIND_POLICY.sse.timeout` drives `server.timeout(req, 0)`, so Bun will not time the request out either. The upstream premise rests on the project's own attestation at packages/site/src/index.ts L168-170 ('`idleTimeout` keeps Bun's keepalive pings landing inside nginx's 60s `proxy_read_timeout`, which would otherwise drop every idle tab') — nginx's `proxy_read_timeout` is a between-successive-reads timer, so a stream that emits nothing for 60s is exactly what it kills. The client is a plain `EventSource` (QueueWidget.svelte L22) with no `retry:` hint, so the browser auto-reconnects after its default delay, giving continuous ~60s connect/drop churn on an idle viewer plus a few seconds per cycle in which queue events are missed permanently (after hydration the stream is the only source of counter updates). Two caveats temper it: the nginx configuration is not in the repo, so that premise is author-attested rather than verified; and the 'compounding the leak' sub-claim does not hold — the proxy closing the upstream socket is a client abort from Bun's perspective, so `cancel()` fires and the three listeners are removed on each cycle. Net: a real robustness defect with low user-visible impact, which is what BUG already denotes. The suggested fix (initial snapshot plus a 20-30s keep-alive cleared in the existing `onClose`) matches what `/sse/admin/stock` gets for free by pushing every 1.5s.

The arithmetic and the mechanism both hold. `pendingJobs()` (L18-24) evicts any front entry older than 60s, and the array is a positional FIFO with no job identity, while `settle` (L31-35) does an unconditional `pendingSince.shift()`. I confirmed the throughput assumption against the backend: `concurrency: 2` maps to bun-boss `localConcurrency: 2` with `batchSize: 1` (queue.ts L1086-1089), and bun-boss's `burstWhileNonEmpty` defaults on (manager.ts, resolveInterval) so a backlog drains at fetch rate with no poll gap — with `Bun.sleep(500 + Math.random()*1500)` that is ~1.6 jobs/s, i.e. ~62s (worst case 100s) to drain the 100-job cap, which exceeds PENDING_TTL_MS. Past a backlog of ~96 the oldest entries age out while their jobs are still legitimately queued; each such eviction decrements the count once, and the job's later completion shifts a newer, still-valid entry, so the undercount compounds. Because `reserveNotificationSlot()` (L59) gates admission on the same counter, MAX_PENDING_NOTIFICATION_JOBS stops being a real bound under sustained overload and the in-memory job table grows. The comment at L13-14 that justifies the TTL ('Jobs here take under two seconds') genuinely conflates processing time with queue residency, which is the root cause. Reachability is as described: one IP is capped at 60 POST/min (1/s, below the 1.6/s drain), so it needs a couple of distinct clients, and the state self-heals on full drain since `shift()` on an empty array is a no-op. I also confirmed the existing test (queue.server.test.ts L22-36) only emits a single `queue:added` and fast-forwards `Date.now`, so it cannot catch this. The recommended `Map<jobId, enqueuedAt>` is the right fix — the payloads already carry `jobId` (events.ts MochiQueueAddedEvent/CompletedEvent/FailedEvent).

The framework-level claim is exactly right. `makeHandler` emits `queue:failed` from its catch on every attempt, carrying `attempt: raw.retryCount + 1` (queue.ts L576), whereas `queue:added` is emitted only from the producer methods (L598, L617), never on a retry. bun-boss's `failJobsBody` retries while `retry_count < retry_limit` (manager.ts ~L1513 / plans.ts failJobsBody), and the stored default is `retry_limit: 2` (plans.ts QUEUE_DEFAULTS L61) — Mochi mirrors that default and this descriptor declares no `retryLimit`, so a job failing every attempt produces one `queue:added` and three `queue:failed`, i.e. one push and three shifts, retiring two other in-flight jobs' entries. So the one-in/one-out assumption encoded in `settle` (subscribed to both `queue:completed` and `queue:failed`, L36-37) is unsound, and it also decrements on a non-terminal failure while the job is still pending. I agree with the reporter's own scoping that this is latent rather than live: the processor (L43-53) does `Bun.sleep`, an array push/shift and an increment, with `job.data.user` always populated by `enqueueNotification`, so there is no throw path, and expiry-based failures are raised by bun-boss's supervisor rather than by `makeHandler`, so they emit no Mochi event. That matters for prioritisation, but the defect is real in code that files.ts publishes verbatim as demo/template source, where it will be copied into processors that do throw. Distinct from F4: different trigger (event multiplicity vs TTL-vs-residency) and separately fixable, even though the suggested jobId-keyed Map happens to cure both.

The leak itself is verified end to end. Both token pages take the token from the query string (L88, L110) and render through the normal shell; packages/support/src/shell.html contains `{{mochi.analytics}}`; `analytics({ exclude: [NEWSLETTER_EMBED_PATH] })` (index.ts L41) excludes only `/newsletter/embed`, and packages/shared/src/index.ts injects the tracker for any non-excluded path whenever `MOCHI_DOCKER === 'true'` — which Dockerfile.production sets (L75), the image used to deploy this package. analyticsTracker.html sets only `data-website-id` and `data-performance`, not `data-exclude-search`, and Umami's documented behaviour is to collect the query string unless that attribute is set (it was added in v2.11.0), so the full token-bearing URL is POSTed to u.khromov.se and persisted there. I also confirmed `unsubscribe_token` is never rotated — only `subInsertStmt` ever writes it; `subReArmStmt` refreshes `confirm_token` but not the unsubscribe one — and that TokenPage.svelte already carries `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`, so the exposure class was recognised and this channel simply missed. One correction to the impact narrative: the pageview that logs a token is the same request that performs the action, so a logged `confirm_token` is already spent (a replay hits the `status === 'confirmed'` branch and returns 'already'), and a logged `unsubscribe_token` has already been used. The residual capability is narrower than stated — the never-rotated unsubscribe token can re-unsubscribe anyone who later re-subscribes, and any future flow change (or a prefetch-then-log ordering) re-opens the rest. I keep MEDIUM because writing live capability tokens into an off-origin analytics store with its own access model is the finding class (CWE-598/532) and the fixes offered — adding both paths to `exclude`, `data-exclude-search`, and redirecting to a bare result page — are all cheap and correct.

The asymmetry is real and sits directly against the invariant the code documents for itself at db.server.ts L257-259. The HTTP responses are indistinguishable — `already` and `created` both fall through to the bare `success()` at L76 — but L66 gates `appendNewsletterLog()` and the awaited `newsletterEmailQueue.add()` on `outcome.kind !== 'already'`, so an address that is a confirmed subscriber short-circuits both. The delta is larger than it first looks: the log insert commits on support.sqlite, and the queue insert commits on a separate SQLite file that Mochi opens with no WAL/synchronous pragma (queue.ts L494, and bun-boss's adapter sets only `foreign_keys` and `busy_timeout`), so the non-`already` path pays extra fsyncing commits plus serialization behind the worker's in-flight queries — a millisecond-scale mean shift, not microseconds. The sampling model also holds up: `requestSubscription` checks the cooldown ahead of the confirmed branch (so the response shape stays uniform), which leaves one clean sample per address per RESEND_COOLDOWN_MS, about 12/hour, comfortably inside the 20-POST/10-min limit and its 3-strike ban, at 19 bits of PoW per probe (DEFAULT_CAPTCHA_BITS) — and an attacker-owned control address exercises the non-`already` path on every probe, cancelling network drift. Probing a confirmed address is side-effect-free as claimed. Honest caveats: the signal must be recovered from internet jitter, so hundreds of interleaved samples per address are needed, and every probe of a non-subscriber mails that address a confirmation, so the campaign is noisy. It stays a true positive because nothing in the code closes the channel, and the suggested fix (always log and enqueue, letting jobs.server.ts L35's `status !== 'pending'` guard no-op the `already` case, or normalise to a fixed response floor) is cheap.

Every link in the chain verifies. `claim()` is `UPDATE … SET email_status='sending' WHERE id=? AND email_status='pending'` (db.server.ts L136), and the only releases are `noteAttemptError` (reachable solely from the inner catch when `Mochi.email` throws) and `requeue` (admin resend via `refreshConfirmToken`, L343) — abnormal termination is neither. packages/support/src/index.ts sets no `queueShutdownTimeout`, so `mountQueues` applies DEFAULT_QUEUE_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT = 10_000 (queue.ts L229, L1065), and the framework's own test asserts the consequence: after the budget expires the job is left not-completed (queueWorker.test.ts L243-280). bun-boss then recovers it — `supervise` defaults true at a 60s interval (attorney.ts L387, L642) and `failJobsByTimeout` re-inserts an `active` job past `started_on + expire_seconds` as `retry` while `retry_count < retry_limit` (plans.ts L1743, failJobsBody); this queue leaves `expireInSeconds` at the 900s default. The retry then reaches L41, `claimNewsletterSend` returns false because the row is still 'sending', and the processor logs `{ event: 'sent', detail: 'Skipped — another job already handled this confirmation' }` and resolves, so bun-boss completes the job and never retries: the confirmation is silently never delivered and the log labels the loss 'sent'. I am downgrading from HIGH_BUG for three reasons the write-up misses or overstates. The trigger needs an abnormal termination inside the seconds-wide claim→markSent window (SIGKILL/OOM/crash, or a SIGTERM with a send outlasting 10s — 'routinely exceeds 10s' overstates a typical SMTP delivery). It is not undiagnosable: EmailLogDialog renders the row's `email_status`, so the subscriber sits visibly at 'email sending', and the log detail says 'Skipped'. And there is a third release path the finding does not mention — a user re-submitting after the cooldown hits `subReArmStmt`, which resets `email_status='pending'` with a fresh token and enqueues a new job, so the affected person recovers by trying again. The stale-claim fix (a `claimed_at` staleness window) and the distinct 'skipped' log event are both still the right changes.

Both halves are straightforwardly correct. `Number('0')` is 0 and therefore falsy, so `NEWSLETTER_RESEND_COOLDOWN_MS=0` and `NEWSLETTER_CONFIRM_TTL_DAYS=0` are discarded in favour of the 5-minute / 14-day defaults — an operator who tries to disable the resend cooldown in staging gets silently ignored, and both knobs are documented, operator-facing variables in packages/support/.env.example (lines 64 and 66), so this is a supported configuration surface rather than a hypothetical. A negative value is truthy and passes through: with `NEWSLETTER_CONFIRM_TTL_DAYS=-1`, `requestSubscription` stores `confirm_expires_at = now + negative` (db.server.ts L267), the confirm route's `confirm_expires_at <= Date.now()` check (routes.ts L98) returns 'expired' on the recipient's first click, and `purgeExpiredPendingSubscribers` — which selects `status='pending' AND confirm_expires_at < ?` (db.server.ts L241) — deletes every new signup on the next nightly cron run. Signup breaks completely and silently, and index.ts's `mochi:init` hook validates only ADMIN_PASSWORD, SMTP_HOST and MOCHI_ORIGIN, so there is no boot-time guard. The house-pattern argument also checks out verbatim: adminAuth.ts L31-34 carries exactly the quoted comment and uses `Number.isFinite(configured) && configured >= 0`. This is operator-triggered rather than attacker-triggered, which is what BUG severity already reflects; the recommended `Number.isFinite && >= 0` parse (or a boot-time throw on a negative TTL) is the correct fix.
